info.name: AI-Powered EMR Assistant — Backend API
info.description:
Complete API collection for the AI-Powered EMR Assistant backend, organised in clinical workflow order (UC-01 through UC-09).

SETUP
1. Start PostgreSQL.
2. Start the main app:            .\.venv\Scripts\uvicorn.exe app.main:app
3. Start the simulated EMR:       .\.venv\Scripts\uvicorn.exe simulated_emr_service.main:app --port 8001
4. Select the 'EMR Assistant — Local' environment, or use the collection variables below.

RUNNING THE WHOLE WORKFLOW
Run the requests top to bottom. Register and Login store the JWT automatically; every later request captures the ids it creates (session_id, note_id, section_id, suggestion_id) into collection variables, so no manual copying is required.

NOTE ON TIMING
Transcription runs in the background and takes roughly 3.5 seconds per 30 seconds of audio on CPU. After 'Stop Recording', poll 'Get Transcript' until status is 'completed' before generating a SOAP note.

STD MAPPING
TC-01 Start Recording          -> 4. Start Recording
TC-02 Stop Recording + Audio   -> 5. Stop Recording (Upload Audio)
TC-06 Diarized Transcript      -> 6. Get Transcript
TC-07 SOAP Draft Generated     -> 8. Generate SOAP Note
TC-03 Edit Draft Saved         -> 10. Edit SOAP Section
TC-08 Code Suggestions Ranked  -> 11/12. Generate / Get Code Suggestions
TC-04 Note Signed and Locked   -> 14. Sign SOAP Note
TC-09 Sync Success             -> 15. Get Sync Status
TC-10 Sync Failure             -> stop the simulated EMR service, then sign a note
TC-05 Retention Policy         -> 16. Trigger Retention Sweep

request.description: Confirms the API is up. Expects {"status": "ok"}.
Creates a doctor account. Returns 201. A duplicate email returns 400 — change the 'email' collection variable to re-run.
OAuth2 password flow. Note this is form-encoded, not JSON. The returned access_token is stored in the 'token' variable and used by every subsequent request.
UC-01 precondition. Creates a session in state INITIATED, bound to the authenticated doctor.
UC-01. Transitions the session to RECORDING. Calling it twice, or on a session in the wrong state, returns a 4xx rather than a 500.

formdata.description: Select a .wav/.m4a/.mp3 file. Accepted content types: audio/wav, audio/mpeg, audio/mp4, audio/x-m4a, audio/ogg, audio/webm. Max duration 30 minutes.

request.description:
UC-02, FR-01. Uploads the consultation audio, stores its metadata, moves the session to STOPPED, and triggers background transcription.

YOU MUST ATTACH A FILE: open the Body tab and select an audio file for the 'file' field. docs/evidence/load_clip.wav works.

UC-06, FR-02. Returns the diarized transcript. Status moves from 'processing' to 'completed'.

Re-send this request until status is 'completed'. Roughly 3.5 seconds per 30 seconds of audio on CPU. Every segment must carry a speaker_role of DOCTOR or PATIENT.

exec: pm.test('Every segment has a speaker role', () =>
console.log('Status is ' + j.status + ' — send this request again.');

request.description: UC-06 alternate flow: ASR failed. Re-runs transcription for this session. Only needed if step 6 reported status 'failed'.

UC-07, FR-03. Builds the SOAP draft from the transcript.

Pipeline is extractive, not generative: PATIENT segments go to SUBJECTIVE deterministically; DOCTOR segments are classified into OBJECTIVE / ASSESSMENT / PLAN by ClinicalBERT. Empty categories fall back to 'Not documented in dialogue.' Exactly four sections are always produced.
Retrieves the SOAP note for this session, with all four sections. Section content is encrypted at rest and decrypted transparently on read.
UC-03, FR-05. The doctor edits a section. Updates last_edited_at. Rejected with 409 once the note is SIGNED — try re-sending this after step 14 to confirm immutability.

UC-08, FR-04. Two independent semantic searches: the ASSESSMENT section against ICD-10 codes only, and the PLAN section against CPT codes only. Results are merged with sequential gap-free ranks, ICD-10 first.

Regenerating on a DRAFT replaces existing suggestions. Regenerating on a SIGNED note returns 409.
Returns the stored suggestions ordered by rank, each with code, description, code_type, confidence_score and accepted flag.
UC-08 requires suggestions to be reviewable and editable. Sets accepted true or false. Only accepted codes are sent to the EMR on sync. Rejected with 409 once the note is signed.

UC-04, FR-06. Creates a Signature, sets the note to SIGNED, sets sync_status to PENDING, and queues EMR synchronisation as a background task.

Signing twice returns 409 — prevented at database level by a unique constraint.

UC-09, FR-07. Returns PENDING, SUCCESS or FAILED.

TC-09: with the simulated EMR running on port 8001, expect SUCCESS within a second or two.
TC-10: stop the simulated EMR service, sign a different note, and expect FAILED — the signed note and its signature must remain intact.

UC-05, FR-08. Development aid: runs the retention sweep on demand instead of waiting for the scheduler.

Audio is only deleted when the note is SIGNED, sync_status is SUCCESS, the flag is older than RETENTION_WINDOW_MINUTES (4), and it has not already been deleted. The signed note, its signature and the transcript are never touched.
Returns the authenticated doctor. Useful for confirming the JWT is valid. Without a token this returns 401.

The simulated EMR service exposes only POST /simulated-emr/records, which the sync client calls; there is no list endpoint. This request opens its interactive docs page instead.

To verify a note arrived, query the database directly:
  psql -U postgres -d simulated_emr -c "SELECT id, source_session_id, source_soap_note_id, received_at FROM simulated_emr_records ORDER BY id DESC LIMIT 5;"
